analyzed_vuln.description: decode_tilehdr() allocates num_samples and contains_subframe as fixed-size stack arrays indexed by c in [0, s->num_channels). It does not validate that s->num_channels <= WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS before using c as an index, so when stream/header state yields a larger channel count, the loop reads/writes past these arrays (ASan shows read overflow at num_samples[c] in line 361). The root cause is missing channel-count bounds enforcement at this function’s array use boundary.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via the WMALOSSLESS decoder fuzz harness, crafted packet/header state must set decoder context with s->num_channels greater than WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS. decode_frame() calls decode_tilehdr() early for each frame; decode_tilehdr then iterates c < s->num_channels and accesses local arrays sized WMALL_MAX_CHANNELS, causing stack OOB during tile header parsing even with tiny/empty payload-derived bitstream data.
